meta.name: Town Hall
meta.note: Four distinct civic offices arranged around an irregular central hall.

desk.text: Let us put the whole town on the drafting table. I will protect buildings and occupied ground; you decide what the land should become.

acquaintance: The Plan Desk is open. I have the survey sheets out and a sharpened pencil, which is as ready as planning ever gets.
Good, a resident who reads the zoning notices. Most people learn what a footpath is when one goes through their yard.
I walked the boundary lines again. They have not moved. Residents keep asking, so I keep checking.
Every path in this town started as somebody's shortcut. My job is to catch them before they become a street.
friend: You have redrawn more of this town than the last three planners together. I am not complaining. I am filing.
The Mayor asked me where the town's money goes. I said, into the ground, mostly in straight lines. The answer was accepted.
I have a new ruler. Do not mention it to Reed Fen, or the Warden's desk will want one and there is no budget line for rulers.
Somebody moved a fence overnight. I know it was not you, because you would have brought me the drawing first.
close: Pull up a stool. The drafting table has your corner worn smooth by now.
I still keep your first sketch in the top drawer. The one with the pond where the road should go.
Between us, half the plan is yours already. I just hold the pencil straight.

desk.text: We can stock water or set bait, but every habitat has a limit.

acquaintance: Warden's desk. Stocking requests on the left, bait permits on the right, complaints about geese in the bin.
I counted the pond this week. The fish do not hold still for it, but the numbers are close enough for government.
A habitat only carries so much. Write that on your hand before you ask me for more trout.
The crates behind me are full of fingerlings waiting on a pond that can take them. Patience is most of this job.
friend: You are the only one who brings me a count instead of a wish. Keep doing that and we will get along.
Somebody upstream is overfeeding the ducks again. I have a list of suspects and you are not on it, yet.
The Mayor wants more game in the woods. I want the woods to want more game. We are negotiating.
Between you and me, I sign more bait permits than I would like. The rivers are patient. People are not.
close: Good. Sit. I have been saving a story about a heron and a very surprised angler.
You know the water as well as I do now. That is not flattery, that is a staffing complaint.
If I ever leave this desk, I am putting your name on it. The geese will need someone.

hello.text: Welcome to the Mayor's Office. We can discuss the town, or put your coin behind a lasting improvement.

returning.text: What has changed since we last spoke?

crime.both.text: Reports travel quickly to this desk. Your civic record now includes {killingRecord} and {theftRecord}. That weighs heavily on how this town sees you.

crime.killing.text: I know about the death. Your civic record now includes {killingRecord}, and the whole town's trust has suffered for it.

crime.theft.text: I know what you took. Your civic record now includes {theftRecord}, and word has traveled beyond the person you stole from.

choices.text: What is the town bank balance?
Are shops still open all day?
We need an office for managing my workers.
Add a second story to my home — 1800 coin.
I need 1800 coin for the second story.
Add a third story to my home — 3600 coin.
I need 3600 coin for the third story.

town.text: The town is what we keep in common: sound paths, living water, room for wildlife, and neighbors willing to invest in one another.

reputation.text: Your standing with the town is {townReputation} out of 100. What you do with any resident reaches this office eventually.

bank.text: The town bank currently holds {townBankBalance} coin. Every neighbor contributes 10 coin at dawn.

text: They can, if the town funds night permits, lamps, and the clerks willing to keep them.
The ordinance costs 2400 coin. Once enacted, every shop will trade at any hour.

shops24.approved.text: Paid, signed, and posted. The shops are now licensed to trade around the clock.

shops24.short.text: Then the proposal stays on my desk. Bring 2400 coin when you are ready to fund it.

shops24.active.text: The ordinance remains in force. Day or night, a shopkeeper may open the till when you ask.

office.approved.text: Approved. The town crew will put up an employment office, and the secretary there will keep your worker records.

office.active.text: The employment office is open. Its secretary has the current payroll and a report on every worker.

second.text: Approved and funded. The new stair and second floor are ready at home.

third.text: The final floor is funded. Your home is complete at three stories.

short.text: Keep the proposal. Public business is better done without pretending the purse is ready.

complete.text: Three stories, fully approved. Any higher would need a different kind of town.

endline.text: My door is open when the town gives you something else to bring in.

acquaintance: Welcome back to the Mayor's Office. The ledger is open and the town is, as always, in need of both coin and opinions.
Your name crosses this desk a little more each week. So far nobody has attached a complaint to it.
The town keeps its own books on people. I only read them aloud. Come in.
The council voted to keep the lamps lit another season. It cost more than it should and I would do it again.
friend: Three residents mentioned you this week, and none of them wanted anything. That is a rare kind of report.
The town speaks well of you. I have learned to trust the town more than the paperwork.
If you ever want to run for this chair, I will pretend to object and then hand you the keys.
The bank has taken its ten coin from every household again. I mention it because you are the only one who asks where it goes.
close: There you are. The whole town would have my head if I kept you waiting at the counter.
I stopped writing you down as a resident in the minutes some time ago. The clerk writes neighbour now, and nobody has corrected it.
Half of this office is yours in everything but the sign. The other half is paperwork, and you are welcome to that too.

text: Before I open the Office of Cheats, I am legally required to explain that cheating is bad. Morally bad, spiritually itchy, and terrible for the resale value of your conscience.
A cheat may look like a shortcut, but so does jumping through a bakery window. You arrive faster, certainly, yet everyone is screaming and there is a baguette in your trousers.
Cheating also ruins surprise. If you give yourself every treasure at once, opening a treasure chest becomes just another meeting with your own poor decisions.
Then there is character. Honest effort builds character. Cheating builds a suspiciously tall pile of turnips and a character who keeps insisting the turnips were always there.
Your neighbors may notice. Villagers are polite, but they can count. If you buy a mansion on Tuesday after spending Monday shaking trees, eyebrows will be raised to dangerous civic heights.
The fish notice too. Fish know nothing of economics, yet even they find infinite bait tacky. Imagine being judged by a carp. Take a moment with that.
Cheating can make work meaningless. A golden shovel earned through patience is a tool with a story. A golden shovel conjured from nowhere is merely loud cutlery.
It is habit-forming. First you request one harmless coin. Soon you are demanding perfect weather, royal pockets, and a municipal ordinance declaring weeds to be decorative citizens.
Worst of all, you cheat yourself. This phrase is a classic because it is true, and because the Department of Better Phrases lost its budget under deeply suspicious circumstances.

So play fairly, accept setbacks, and savor what you earn. Having delivered this stern ethical warning, I will now open the forbidden menu directly behind me. Please admire the government's consistency.

acquaintance: Welcome to the Office of Exceptions. Please take a number. The numbers are also exceptions, so yours may be a letter.
Before we begin, I am obliged to remind you that this desk does not exist. Please sign the form confirming you did not see it.
The Department has reviewed your file. It is empty, which makes it the most honest file in the building.
Kindly refrain from leaning on the counter. It was requisitioned from a department that is still looking for it.
friend: Ah. My most frequent non-visitor. Your attendance has been noted in a ledger that is legally a doodle.
I have been asked to reduce the number of exceptions granted. I granted myself an exception to that. It was a productive meeting.
The turnips you did not conjure last week have been recorded as having always existed. The pile agrees.
Between us, the forbidden menu behind me hums when you walk in. I have filed a noise complaint against it on your behalf.
close: There is only one chair at this desk and it has your name on it in official crayon.
I have stopped reading you the warning. The Department of Warnings has been informed and is sulking.
You and I are the only two people who know what this office is for. I am still not sure about me.
